Understanding Modern Neural Architectures

Alice Johnson April 15, 2026

Neural networks have evolved substantially over the past decade, progressing from simple convolutional architectures to complex transformer models with billions of parameters. In this article, we examine key design patterns and architectural tradeoffs.

One of the central innovations in modern transformer models is multi-head self-attention. Self-attention enables tokens across an entire sequence to attend to each other simultaneously, overcoming the sequential bottlenecks inherent in recurrent architectures.

Furthermore, feed-forward sublayers with gated linear activations allow the network to model highly nonlinear relationships in the representation space. When combined with residual stream connections and layer normalization, deep models can be trained stably without vanishing gradients.

Modern architectures also leverage mixture-of-experts (MoE) routing to scale parameter count while maintaining constant inference FLOPs per token. By routing tokens dynamically to specialized sub-networks, capacity expands significantly.
